summary.text: Rob Consalvo is a Democratic state representative from the 14th Suffolk District who has served in the Massachusetts House of Representatives since January 2021 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Before joining the House he served 12 years on the Boston City Council, and he began his career as an aide to Senator Edward M. Kennedy.

paragraphs.text: Rob Consalvo graduated from Catholic Memorial High School in 1987 and from Xavier University in Cincinnati, Ohio, with a degree in political science.

He began in public service as an intern and later staff assistant and press assistant in the offices of Senator Edward M. Kennedy, and also worked as a legislative aide to State Representative Angelo M. Scaccia.

Consalvo was elected to the Boston City Council in a 2002 special election and served 12 years as the District 5 councilor, representing Hyde Park, Readville, Roslindale and Mattapan; he chaired the council's committees on Public Safety, Housing and Ways and Means.
He later became Deputy Director of the City of Boston's Boston Home Center and worked as a senior advisor to the Boston Public Schools superintendent.
Consalvo succeeded Scaccia in the House and took office on January 6, 2021.

He represents Hyde Park, Roslindale, Readville and West Roxbury, and currently serves as vice chair of the House Committee on Rules and the Joint Committee on Rules and as a member of the Joint Committees on Housing and on Labor and Workforce Development.
His official biography says he lives in Hyde Park with his wife, Michelle, and their three children, who attend Boston Public Schools.
